analysis.one_liner: Pidilite makes adhesives, sealants and construction chemicals (Fevicol, M-seal, Dr. Fixit, Araldite) sold to households, carpenters and contractors (Consumer & Bazaar) as well as industrial customers (B2B).
tags: Margin hit by raw material spike
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results (quarter ended 30 Sept 2026) were reported on 28 Oct 2026: consolidated revenue grew roughly 21% year-on-year, but EBITDA margin fell sharply as vinyl acetate monomer (VAM, a key raw material) spiked to around $1,630/ton before easing to about $1,200/ton. Standalone PAT still grew about 10% YoY despite the cost shock. Next results (Q3 FY27) are expected mid-to-late January 2027, though no board meeting date is confirmed yet.
analysis.plain_terms: Pidilite is the Fevicol company - almost every Indian household or carpenter has used one of its products, and it also sells industrial chemicals to factories. Sales are growing well, around 21% in the latest quarter, driven by actual volume growth rather than just price hikes. But profitability took a hit this quarter because one of its key raw materials got a lot more expensive, and that cost hasn't been fully passed on to customers yet. The real question is whether that raw material cost settles down or keeps swinging.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (June 2026 quarter): standalone EBITDA margin was a healthy 26.3%. Q2 FY27 (Sept 2026 quarter): standalone EBITDA margin dropped to about 20.4% and consolidated to about 20.5%, a sharp sequential fall, because VAM prices roughly doubled during the quarter before partly cooling off. This is a genuine raw-material cost swing, not an accounting reclassification - PAT still grew (~7-10% YoY) because volumes and price hikes offset much of the hit. Underlying volume growth was 10.7% consolidated (Consumer & Bazaar 11.1%, B2B 9.2%), so this is real demand growth, not just price-led. Management has taken price hikes of 12-15% in Q1 plus another 3-5% in October and is targeting an EBITDA margin corridor of 20-24% for the rest of the year. Revenue figures vary slightly by source (₹4,285-4,298 crore consolidated) - treat as rounding differences, not a real discrepancy.
analysis.performance_read: Over 1 year the stock is down only 0.96% while the Nifty fell 10.92% - Pidilite has held up better than the market recently. Over 3 years (21.21% vs Nifty 20.83%) it has roughly tracked the index, and over 5 years (27.17% vs Nifty 28.58%) it has slightly lagged. The stock is currently 14.1% below its 12 Aug 2026 peak of ₹1,701.5, and down 9.3% over the last 3 months versus a 5.46% Nifty fall - so recent underperformance is real, not a corporate-action artifact. A 2:1 bonus issue took effect on 23 Sept 2025 and is already reflected in the adjusted price series used here, so it does not explain any of this price fall. The broader pattern - a well-run, profitable company whose stock has roughly matched a weak Nifty over 3-5 years - points to a valuation that has been quietly de-rating even as the underlying business kept growing.
analysis.valuation_read: The stock trades at roughly 55-58x trailing earnings and about 13x book value. That is cheap relative to Pidilite's own history - its 10-year average P/E is near 71x and its 5-year average near 82x - but it is not cheap in absolute terms; it remains one of the most richly valued large-cap industrials in India. Why it looks 'cheaper': the market has been steadily de-rating the stock over the past 2-3 years (P/E fell from ~103x in FY22 to ~53x in FY26) as growth normalised from pandemic-era highs. Whether that de-rating is complete, or whether margin volatility like this quarter's VAM spike justifies a further de-rating, is a separate and open question.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is genuinely volume-led, not just price-led: consolidated underlying volume growth was 10.7% in the latest quarter, with both the consumer business (11.1%) and the B2B business (9.2%) contributing. Price hikes (roughly 15-20% cumulatively over the year) have added to revenue on top of this, but the volume numbers show real demand, which is the more durable kind of growth in a business exposed to commodity input costs.
analysis.health_read: Balance sheet risk is minimal - total debt is only around ₹351 crore against a market cap near ₹1.49 lakh crore, so the company is effectively debt-free, and ROE (23.9%) and ROCE (31%) are both strong. The real risk here is business risk, not financial risk: margins are exposed to swings in VAM (vinyl acetate monomer) and other petrochemical-linked raw material prices, as this quarter showed directly. Profit-to-cash conversion was not independently verified in this check - not verified, check cash flow statement on Screener.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters hold about 69.2% of the company, essentially unchanged recently, with zero pledged shares - consistent with Pidilite's long clean history on this front. Foreign institutional holding has drifted down slightly over the last four quarters (from about 12.1% to 11.7%), while domestic mutual fund holding has also edged down marginally, with LIC Mutual Fund a small exception that has been quietly adding. No single marquee individual investor (of the kind sometimes seen in other Indian consumer stocks) shows up on the register in the sources checked - not verified beyond what's listed here, check the latest shareholding filing on BSE/NSE for the full list.
